page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-24 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The configuration includes 90.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. The CPU features support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 extensions) as well as Intel AMX matrix acceleration instructions (amx_tile and amx_int8). The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results place the c4-standard-24 primarily in the middle 50% tier across multi-purpose compute, memory, and database workloads. It recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 13,690.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 34,968.15, alongside a stress-ng multi-core CPU result of 21,669.81. Notably strong performance appears in text and image handling, where Geekbench image processing reached 13,744.0 and text processing scored 2,618.0, placing both metrics in the top 25%. LLM inference text generation using a small 135M parameter model reached 396.71 tokens per second, qualifying in the top 10% tier, benefiting directly from modern vector and matrix instruction availability.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a balanced compute-to-memory footprint suitable for workloads requiring substantial RAM density without paying for high-tier compute-optimized clock speeds. Tradeoffs include reliance on networked block storage due to the absence of bundled local NVMe disks, as well as the absence of hardware accelerators for larger AI models, where medium 7B model generation drops to 17.23 tokens per second. The instance is suited for enterprise application servers, mid-tier database operations, Clang software compilation pipelines, and containerized microservice backends.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-24 is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 24 dedicated vCPUs (12 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. It is paired with 90.0 GB of memory (3.75 GB per vCPU) and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. The instance features vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, but provides no integrated local storage or GPUs. Performance testing reflects middle-tier output for PassMark CPU (34,968.15) and Geekbench multi-core (13,690.0) metrics, with above-average results in Geekbench image and text processing. Small-model LLM generation reaches top-tier throughput at 396.71 tokens per second. With balanced resource ratios, the c4-standard-24 fits enterprise web backends, CI/CD compilation, and mid-tier databases requiring networked block storage.
